resources.string: A11y Speech Logger
A11y Focus Logger
Logs accessibility focus, window changes and announcements under the A11ySpeech logcat tag, and dumps the screen\'s node tree on request.
Read what TalkBack says

A11y Speech Logger writes to logcat exactly what TalkBack says and which element it is talking about, so a person or an LLM can audit an app\'s accessibility from text. Set it up once with the steps below, then capture sessions from your computer.

What does it capture?

Two components write to the A11ySpeech logcat tag, one record per line: [kind] t=<ms> <fields>.

• A silent text-to-speech engine logs every utterance as [speech]. While it is the default engine, TalkBack is silent on the whole device.
• The A11y Focus Logger accessibility service logs the focused element as [focus] (id, class, text, role, state, size and heuristic issues such as NO_LABEL or SMALL_TARGET), plus [window] changes, [announce] announcements and [tree] node-tree dumps on request.

How do I enable the A11y Focus Logger?

Turn on A11y Focus Logger in the accessibility settings, usually under installed apps or services. Leave its shortcut off: on some devices enabling the shortcut turns TalkBack off. To do it from a computer, see the next question.
How do I turn TalkBack on or off from adb?
